title: IPv6 Prefix Options for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) version 6
summary: Defines DHCPv6 options for delegating IPv6 prefixes automatically. A delegating router, typically an ISP's, hands a long-lived prefix to a requesting router across an administrative boundary, without needing to know the topology of the links where the prefix will be used. It has been replaced by RFC 8415.

plainLanguage.summary: DHCPv6 prefix delegation lets one router request an IPv6 prefix from another router. The requesting router can then divide the assigned prefix among its own links.

questions: how does an isp delegate an ipv6 prefix
what are dhcpv6 option codes 25 and 26
subtitle: How a DHCPv6 server delegates IPv6 prefixes to a requesting router.

tldr.problem: A provider needs a way to assign an IPv6 address prefix to a customer's router without knowing the layout of the customer's internal links.
tldr.mechanism: DHCPv6 uses an IA_PD option to group delegated prefixes and an IA_PD Prefix option to carry each prefix and its lifetimes.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3633 has been obsoleted by RFC 8415. RFC 6603 and RFC 7550 updated it.

today: RFC 3633 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 8415. It was updated by RFC 6603 and RFC 7550.

sections.title: Delegating an IPv6 Prefix
sections.content:
RFC 3633 adds DHCPv6 options for assigning IPv6 prefixes to requesting routers. The delegating router chooses a prefix based on the requester's identity and does not need to know how the requester will use it internally.

The RFC describes provider-to-customer delegation as a typical case. Prefixes are expected to remain stable for a long time, and an old and a replacement prefix may coexist during renumbering.
sections.plainLanguage: A delegating router gives a prefix to a requesting router. The requesting router decides how to use that prefix on its own network.

sections.title: Identity Associations
sections.content:
An Identity Association for Prefix Delegation (IA_PD) groups related prefixes and their configuration information. It is identified by an IAID chosen by the requesting router, and the identifier must remain consistent across that router's restarts.

An IA_PD may apply to the router, a group of interfaces or one interface. Each delegated prefix has preferred and valid lifetimes; the requesting router must stop using a prefix when its valid lifetime expires.
sections.plainLanguage: An IA_PD is a named group that tracks delegated prefixes. Each prefix has a preferred lifetime and a final time after which it must no longer be used.

sections.title: The Prefix Delegation Options
sections.content:
Option code 25, OPTION_IA_PD, carries the IAID, renewal times T1 and T2, and options belonging to that association. It can contain one or more IA_PD Prefix options.

Option code 26, OPTION_IAPREFIX, carries the IPv6 prefix, its length and its preferred and valid lifetimes. A lifetime value of 0xFFFFFFFF means infinity. A requester may provide a prefix or size as a preference, but the delegating router chooses what to assign.
sections.plainLanguage: The IA_PD option identifies a group and when to ask about it again. The IA_PD Prefix option identifies a prefix and how long it can be used.

sections.title: Requesting, Renewing and Releasing Prefixes
sections.content:
A requesting router sends Solicit with an IA_PD option. A delegating router can answer with Advertise; the requester then sends Request and receives a Reply containing the delegated prefix information.

The requester uses Renew or Rebind to extend lifetimes and Release to return a prefix. After receiving a valid Reply, it assigns subnets from the delegated prefix to downstream links, but must not use that prefix on the link through which it received the DHCP message.
sections.plainLanguage: The routers exchange DHCPv6 messages to select and return a prefix. Later, the requesting router asks to extend the prefix lifetime or sends a message to release it.

sections.title: Security and Assigned Codes
sections.content:
A rogue delegating router could provide a false prefix, while repeated requests could exhaust a server's available prefixes. The RFC recommends DHCP authentication between requesting and delegating routers, subject to its stated link assumptions.

IANA assigned code 25 to OPTION_IA_PD, code 26 to OPTION_IAPREFIX and status code 6 to NoPrefixAvail.
sections.plainLanguage: A false prefix can prevent a router from reaching the intended network. Authentication can help the routers check who sent the delegation messages.
